# Exam

Each week we will provide a short task to test your knowledge, these should be used to guide your study for the final exam.

The task is to join some non spatial data to some spatial data.

1. Go to the New Zealand spatial data portal and download the file Territorial Authority 2018 (generalised), these are city or district councils. Make sure it’s the Territorial Authority 2018 data not SA1.

2. Go to the Stats NZ website and download the Statistical area 1 dataset for 2018 for the whole of New Zealand. Download the excel file this week, not the .csv.

3. Unzip the downloaded census file and open 2018-SA1-dataset-individual-part-3a-total-NZ_updated_16-7-20, you will see a tab for Territorial authority. **Join the 2018 paid employee field to the spatial data and make a basic map. Hint, you may need to make a new .csv file from the data.**


# Load data

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
mycsv <- read_csv("homework1_data/edited-2018-SA1-dataset-individual-part-3a-total-NZ_updated_16-7-20.csv")

spec(mycsv)

library(sf)
# my data is within a homework1_data folder.
shape <- st_read("homework1_data/statsnz-territorial-authority-2018-generalised-SHP/territorial-authority-2018-generalised.shp")
```

```{r}
# reproject Coordinate 
shape_nztm <- st_transform(shape, 2193)   # EPSG:2193 = NZGD2000 / NZ Transverse Mercator

summary(shape_nztm)
plot(shape_nztm)


# That plots everything in the shapefile (all the attributes) if you just wanted the geometry (outline of the shape) you could use…

library(sf)
shape_nztm %>% 
  st_geometry() %>%
  plot()
```
# Join data
```{r}
shape_nztm2 <- shape_nztm%>%
  merge(.,
        mycsv,
        by.x="TA2018_V1_",
        by.y="Area_Code")

shape_nztm%>%
  head(., n=10)

'Length:'
nrow(shape_nztm2)
```

## Make thematic map (or a qtm)
```{r}
library(tmap)
tmap_mode("plot")

# change the fill to your column name if different
shape_nztm2 %>%
  qtm(.,fill = "2018_paid_employee")
```
